headline: Iran Currency Crisis: 2 million Iranian rials per dollar, find out how Iran's economy is falling, oil exports nearly halted | Iran Rial Crash Currency Crisis Us Sanctions Economi D Day
summary: The rial fell to a record 2.02 million per US dollar on Monday. The US is preparing new economic sanctions, which the Treasury Secretary has described as "Economic D-Day". Reports say oil exports have nearly halted.
why: Iran's rial exchange rate and oil exports are central to the country's economy, and US sanctions on Iranian oil affect global crude supply and flows.

impacts.name: Iranian rial
impacts.why: The article reports the rial falling to a record low against the dollar.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Reports of a record low for the rial and planned US sanctions that could further restrict Iranian oil exports drive the move.
